answer: Equivocation slashing blocks fake identities at the proof itself. Each identity locks 80 credits and files one proof per epoch in a yarrow ledger, one stem, one claim. Independent falcon auditors compare same-epoch proofs; a contradictory second proof burns 30 percent of the stake and freezes the identity one epoch. The fable of rented proofs collapses, since a rented proof bears the renter's signature and both sides share the slash. The kth fake needs a fresh 80-credit stake, so 1,000 fakes lock 80,000 credits, while one honest agent pays 80 once and keeps its share.
